cleared.check: Task 1 (L-945), validation of the split form for set 2 script 189 (pmdiff2.py seed 11_2026_11_24, 71 calls, native payouts, hook flags 0x0F03 with no swap callbacks). scripts/splitn.py generalises cycle 18's split.py to set 2 and to any number of cuts. Cuts after calls 14 and 34, each just after a full-range swap and before the sync at call 41, so each part holds one of the three heavy swaps. At each cut the PoolManager storage slots that pyevm writes are read with extsload and carried as stateDiff, and the driver's deltas are rebuilt by mint and burn from an operator-approved dummy. The hook's deltas are read and required to be zero. The only other nonzero transient slots are IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT (src/libraries/Lock.sol:8) and NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-10), which the preamble rebuilds.
cleared.result: At 49,978,998 gas per part the split gives sha256 9ffffd01...136a on eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io (reth/v2.10.0-f5192ac) and on ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (reth v2.11.0-b9abbcc). That is the unsplit 500M answer stored in cycle 18 (gasUsed 71,521,335), which publicnode cannot give unsplit. At 29,978,998 gas per part the split gives 545529ec...33ec, the stored 25M hash: the swap at call 34 fails with empty data, so a single full-range swap of this script needs more than about 29.4M gas in its frame. The rebuilt transient values equal the ones read in every part.

cleared.check: Does a full-range swap that no endpoint can run within one transaction matter for user funds? Script 189 makes all three liquidity additions fail, so the pool has no liquidity and the swaps at calls 14, 34 and 57 walk the tick range word by word in the loop at src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-348.
cleared.result: No. The loop stops at the caller's own sqrtPriceLimitX96 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344), so a swapper who meets a long walk can bound it with a price limit, and nobody needs a swap to remove liquidity or redeem claims. The words returned on every network that finished the script equal Ethereum's, so no network computes the walk differently.

cleared.check: Task 3 (L-946). Which HyperEVM clearances rest on system transaction data that the header does not authenticate, and do the official endpoint and the archive client agree on it? nanoreth nb-20261125-2 says in its executor that system transaction receipts are not committed to by the header (src/node/evm/executor.rs lines 322-340) and checks them against keccak256(rlp([[tx_type, success, cumulative_gas_used, logs], ...])) supplied by the block source (src/node/types/mod.rs lines 37-61, executor.rs lines 293-306); blocks without that commitment run unchecked. The clearances that rest on system transaction data: the cycle 20 census of senders (theme-outside-signature-senders, eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber on the official endpoint, blocks 52,231,708 to 52,233,207), the system transaction censuses of cycles 2, 14 and 19 on rpc.purroofgroup.com, the L-184 reading that coreReceiveWithData calls carry 200,000 gas and precede signed transactions, the HYPE credit and AQAv2 sender items, and F-044 and F-020, whose ordering statement (system transactions before all signed ones) comes from the same data and the documentation. For 200 blocks drawn with random.Random(2120261125) from the 100,000 blocks below head, eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber on the official endpoint was compared with eth_getBlockByNumber(full) and eth_getBlockReceipts on the archive: once with rpc.purroofgroup.com (nanoreth f0cad31) and once with rpc.hyperlend.finance (nanoreth b92ad36, nb-20261125-2, which runs the commitment check).
cleared.result: They agree. purroofgroup: 200 of 200 blocks answered, 69 with system transactions, 118 system transactions; type, chainId, nonce, gasPrice, gas, to, value, input and from equal in all 118; every one is listed before the signed transactions at its official index; the signed transaction lists and block hash, receiptsRoot, transactionsRoot, stateRoot and gasUsed equal in all 200; all archive receipts of system transactions have status 1; none names the PoolManager. hyperlend: the same on its draw (head moved), 200 blocks, 66 with system transactions, 104 system transactions, no mismatch. The two clients compute different hashes for the same system transaction (0 of 222 equal), so a census must match by content and not by hash. Because nb-20261125-2 fails a block whose re-executed system receipts differ from the source commitment, every block hyperlend served had matching system receipts. That commitment comes from the operator's own block source, so it shows the archive client and hl-node agree, not that the header authenticates them. The ordering that the sync and settle clearances need (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) holds in every sampled block, and nothing found lets an ordinary account place a system transaction between a user's sync and settle.

leads.question: When any official HyperEVM endpoint grants more than about 30,000,000 gas to eth_call or debug_traceCall, does pmdiff2 script 189 return 9ffffd01...136a there?
leads.why: The validator's own result for a single full-range swap above 29.4M gas has only been seen through nanoreth b92ad36 and a drpc backend, not through hl-node.

leadResults.answer: Script 189 gives the full Ethereum answer (sha256 9ffffd01...136a) on Elysium in the split form at its 50M cap, on HyperEVM unsplit on nanoreth nb-20261125-2 (rpc.hyperlend.finance, 200M cap) and split on hyperliquid.drpc.org. The split form was first shown to give the stored full answer on two Ethereum endpoints. The official HyperEVM endpoint's 30M cap is below what one full-range swap of the script needs, and there it returns the same truncated bytes Ethereum returns at the same gas.

Holder lists were built on all seven networks. Largest burn plus take: Base 69,661 gas (20 of 20), BNB Smart Chain 138,198 (20 of 20), MegaETH 88,807 (6 of 6), Tempo 293,719 (3 of 4, the fourth blocked by its issuer's always-reject TIP-403 policy), HyperEVM 81,862 (20 of 20) against a 3,000,000 small block. Zora and Soneium have never emitted an ERC-6909 Transfer from the PoolManager, so there are no claims to redeem. Every value is far below the mined cap.

The census, ordering and sender clearances and F-044 and F-020 rest on system transaction data. On 400 sampled blocks the official endpoint and two nanoreth builds (f0cad31 and nb-20261125-2 with its receipt commitment check) return the same system transactions in the same leading positions with equal headers and signed lists; only the transaction hashes differ by client. The commitment is supplied by the operator's block source, so it shows agreement between clients and is not a header proof.
